# 14 · Three-Year Award History Automation

Every ten minutes: enrol stored real notices and refresh up to ten eligible OPEN notices serially. Closed notices are preserved without new provider calls. Backend owns durable claims, retry backoff, freshness, three-year history and opening bidders/scores.

KST calendar-day provider budget: 1,000 calls, reset at 00:00 KST, including same-day award and outcome jobs and outstanding reservations. The legacy api_calls_24h and budget_reserved_24h fields now describe this calendar day. Stateless manual company-award searches remain outside the audit ledger; provider quota errors are preserved as incomplete results. Each notice reserves up to 150 calls, reduced to the remaining budget; require at least 50 to start. The entire batch shares 480 seconds; no next notice starts with less than 60 seconds remaining.

Manual execution runs a synthetic offline fixture with zero network calls. Scheduled execution uses only protected award operations, native JSON bodies and the approved W10 Generic Header credential. The historical HTTP node name Refresh One Queued Award Notice is retained exactly for credential binding, but now invokes a bounded batch. No AI, analysis, Teams or direct provider calls exist here. Emergency switch: PAI_LOOP_EMERGENCY_DISABLE=true.

HTTP timeout 520 seconds; no retry or redirect. Final outputs contain validated aggregates only. Identifiers and source rows are omitted; n8n payload storage is disabled. Backend persists audit and progress.
